entries.lesson_title: Fourier Coefficients of a Sine Wave
entries.core_move: Compute the complex Fourier series coefficients of a sine wave by converting it into positive and negative fundamental-frequency complex exponentials and identifying the nonzero harmonic coefficients that determine its magnitude and phase spectra.

entries.lesson_title: Fourier Coefficients of a Rectangular Periodic Signal
entries.core_move: Compute the complex Fourier series coefficients of a rectangular periodic signal by recognizing that only the pulse-support interval contributes to the one-period coefficient integral and evaluating the resulting exponential integral in terms of amplitude, width, period, and harmonic index.
Compute the DC Fourier-series coefficient for a rectangular periodic signal by converting duty cycle and signal levels into the average value over one period.
Identify coefficient cancellations in the Fourier series coefficient formula to determine which even and odd harmonic indices of a periodic signal contribute nonzero spectral components.

entries.lesson_title: Fourier Coefficients of a Periodic Exponential
entries.core_move: Compute the complex Fourier-series coefficient integral for one period of an exponentially shaped periodic signal by combining the signal exponent with the harmonic kernel to obtain each harmonic coefficient.
Compute complex-valued Fourier series coefficients by evaluating the one-period complex-exponential coefficient integral and interpreting each result as the harmonic's amplitude-and-phase weight.

Convert computed complex Fourier series coefficients into a magnitude spectrum by calculating |$c_k$| at DC and each positive and negative harmonic and interpreting the stem plot as the periodic signal's harmonic strength distribution.

Compute and interpret the phase spectrum by extracting the argument of each nonzero complex Fourier series coefficient and aligning those phases with the corresponding positive and negative harmonics of a periodic continuous-time signal.
